rationale: Greek προγνώστης 'one who knows beforehand.' Lycopolitan/Coptic spelling has ⲣⲛ for ⲅⲛ (regular assimilation in this dialect). Used here as the chapter's central question: how does the Mind of Light grasp the elect as foreknowers in the manner of the apostle? Confirmed within the chapter by paraphrase ⲥⲉⲣ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲉϩⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ 'they shall first-know' (lines 33-34). 'Foreknower' preserves the morpheme structure (πρό- + γνωσ-) and the verbal-active sense over generic 'prophet.'

Lycopolitan rendering of Greek εἰκών 'image, likeness.' Prosthetic ϩ- for spiritus + ⲁ for ι (Lyc. vowel-shift). Distinguished from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' (the relational quality) and ⲙⲟⲣⲫⲏ 'form': ϩⲁⲕⲟⲛ here denotes a discrete imprinted image/picture (paralleled with ⲍⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' in line 13 — both as derivative manifestations cast from a higher original). Already attested in glossary as ⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ; this entry documents the spelling variant ϩⲁⲕⲟ́ⲛ.

Verbal idiom: ⲣ̄- ('do') + ϣⲁⲣⲡ ('first') + ⲛⲣⲉϩⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ (agent-noun 'knower' formed on standard ⲣⲉϥ- + ⲥⲟⲟⲩⲛ pattern). Functions as the Coptic equivalent of Greek προγνῶναι. Used here to gloss/explicate ⲡⲣⲟⲣⲛⲱⲥⲧⲏⲥ in the chapter, confirming the morpheme-by-morpheme reading 'first-knowers.' Standard Coptic+Greek doublet structure of the Kephalaia.

Contracted Lycopolitan form of ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲧⲉ 'the upper side' (already in glossary). Distinct from the homograph ⲡⲥⲁⲧⲧ 'the chosen one' (Zarathustra epithet); disambiguation here by spatial-cosmological context (paired with ⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'the lower side' in the immediately following line 7). The contracted form documents another cosmological-spatial register variant alongside ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ and ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲧⲉ.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'reveal, uncover' (already in glossary as ⲟ̄ⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ). The form ⲛⲟ́ⲱⲗⲡ has nominalizing/relative ⲛ- prefix or the qualitative ending. Eschatological-revelatory verb for the Mind of Light's revelation to the elect. Same etymon as ⲟ́ⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ but spelled with ⲛ-onset and ⲟ́ for ⲱ.
